evidence.evidence_text_or_value: To understand the underlying preferences of users and properties of items, various model-based approaches have been developed to learn hidden representations of both users and items (Koren et al., 2009; Xue et al., 2017; Rendle, 2010).

Recent
advancements in edge computing have provided a potential solution through federated learning (FL), which allows
users to collaboratively train models on their local devices
without exposing personal data (McMahan et al., 2017).

Despite its effectiveness in preserving privacy, the above paradigm suffers significant communication and computation overheads as it requires transmission of the full model and complete updates (Bonawitz et al., 2019)

Existing sparsityaware FL protocols reduce communication overhead at the cost of increased privacy leakage (Lin et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2023; Lu et al., 2023), as they inevitably reveal the coordinates of non-zero elements or significantly narrow the set of potential non-zero updates.
To mitigate this risk, secure aggregation (SecAgg) (Bonawitz et al., 2017) is adopted to prevent the server from inspecting individual updates during training
